tests.name: test_nlo_matching_moments_reduce_to_the_analytic_constant
tests.claim: At lam = 2 e^{-gamma_E - 1/2} the pseudo-ITD NLO matching moments equal CF*L(N) exactly for integer N.
tests.actual: Computes _pseudoitd_nlo_moments(orders, lam=that lam) for N=2..5 and compares to a from-scratch harmonic-sum recomputation of L(N) (helper _harmonic, no call to the source's _psi).
tests.how: digamma/trigamma-based B(N),L(N) formula (source, mpmath.fp.psi) vs explicit-summation harmonic numbers (test); real and imaginary parts checked separately; a magnitude floor guards against a vacuous zero target.
tests.catches: a wrong numeric coefficient in B/L (e.g. the 1.5 or a 2.0 prefactor), a sign flip on the log term or on L, an off-by-one in the harmonic-sum order or the N/N-1 argument shift, or a wrong C_F. Would NOT catch an error shared with the B(N)/L(N) derivation itself: that formula is uncited anywhere in this repo (see weaknesses), so the independence is real for the digamma-vs-explicit-sum arithmetic but not for the underlying physics content.

tests.name: test_matching_log_carries_the_lambda_dependence
tests.claim: Away from the log-cancelling lam, the moments move by exactly ln(lam^2 e^{2 gamma_E+1}/4) * B(N).
tests.actual: Subtracts the log-cancelling reference (lam from test 1) from a second call at lam=1.7 and compares the difference to CF*log_factor*B(N), B recomputed via the same from-scratch harmonic-sum helper.
tests.how: reference and got are both outputs of the function under test at two different lam; the lam-independent L(N) term cancels in the subtraction, isolating the log(lam)*B(N) piece against an independently recomputed B(N).
tests.bar: rtol=1e-12, no atol= -> np.allclose's default atol=1e-8 applies and dominates (measured this audit: atol=1e-8 exceeds the rtol contribution by ~3075x at these RHS magnitudes, |rhs| in [3.3, 6.4]); true effective bar is ~1e-8 absolute, not 1e-12 relative
tests.catches: a broken (contour, lam) memoization key (if lam dropped out of the cache key, got would equal reference exactly and the assertion would fail loudly since the RHS is manifestly nonzero); a wrong log_factor argument/exponent; a wrong CF or B(N) coefficient in the lam-dependent term. Does not test the L(N) additive constant (test 1's job) since it cancels; shares the B(N)-formula-uncited caveat with test 1; the true bar is looser than its rtol parameter suggests (see weaknesses).

tests.name: test_pitd_evolve_constant_reaches_the_built_kernels
tests.claim: config.PITD_EVOLVE controls whether build_pseudoitd's main kernel is EvolvedPseudoITD, with matching/matching_order/mu0_2/lam threaded from config.
tests.actual: Monkeypatches PITD_EVOLVE True then False and rebuilds the same lattice record both times; on True, checks isinstance(EvolvedPseudoITD) plus four attribute equalities against config constants; on False, checks NOT isinstance(EvolvedPseudoITD).
tests.how: closure_JAM_truth/closure_NNPDF_truth's build_pseudoitd -> pixel.data.PseudoITD.from_file -> _kernel_for, driven by a real generated manifest record via _lattice_fixture. Parametrized over both suites, whose datasets.py are byte-identical and whose four checked config constants (PITD_EVOLVE, PITD_MATCHING_ORDER, PITD_MATCHING_LAMBDA, Q0_2) also match, so the two parametrizations exercise identical code against two different generated manifests, not two different implementations.
tests.bar: exact isinstance/equality checks; pytest.approx (default rel) on two O(1) float constants
tests.catches: build_pseudoitd dropping the evolution kwargs again (the historical bug this file exists to pin), a swapped config key, or mu0_2/lam not threaded through. Does NOT catch config.ORDER/config.MODE failing to reach kernel.order/kernel.mode (both flow through the same evolution dict but are never compared -- see weaknesses); the False branch does not pin what type the kernel is instead of EvolvedPseudoITD.

tests.name: test_systematic_nuisances_stay_on_the_bare_transform
tests.claim: Lattice-artifact nuisance contributions (ht, chiral, cont_invz, cont_aL, inf_Lz) never become EvolvedPseudoITD, regardless of PITD_EVOLVE, and each has a real coefficient.
tests.actual: Builds the dataset with PITD_EVOLVE=True, splits contributions[0] (physical) from the rest, checks the physical kernel IS EvolvedPseudoITD and every nuisance kernel is NOT, with a non-None coefficient.
tests.how: Same build_pseudoitd path; PseudoITD.from_file routes systematics through _kernel_for(..., coefficient=coeff) with no mu0_2/evolution_lambda, so the split is structural in the source, not merely conventional.
tests.catches: a change that accidentally threads mu0_2/evolution_lambda into the systematics builder too (which would invent DGLAP scale dependence for lattice artifacts that should not have any), or a coefficient factory silently wired to None. Relies on, unasserted, contributions[0] always being the physical field (true by PseudoITD.from_file's list-literal construction order -- see weaknesses).

tests.name: test_matching_changes_the_operator_it_is_applied_to
tests.claim: Matching must not be a silent no-op on the assembled EvolvedPseudoITD transform.
tests.actual: Builds bare (matching=False) and matched (matching="NLO") EvolvedPseudoITD kernels, otherwise identical, and requires their .matrix() outputs to differ by more than 1e-6*scale.
tests.how: Direct kernel construction on a 9-point grid + .matrix() call; pure nonzero-difference structural check, no comparison to any expected value.
tests.catches: matching wired to nothing (a no-op bug), or an exception silently swallowed leaving matched==bare. Measured this audit: actual diff/scale ~= 0.70 at these kinematics, six orders above the bar, so this test alone cannot distinguish correctly-wired matching from wrong-magnitude matching -- only from completely inert matching. The bit-correct composition (Fourier @ matching(mu2) @ evolution(mu2), row by row) is independently checked to rtol=1e-11 in tests/test_evolution.py::test_evolved_pseudoitd_matching_composes_after_evolution, now cross-referenced in this test's docstring.

tests.name: test_li_vector_density_reduces_to_existing_nlo_mellin_coefficient
tests.claim: Li's normalized one-loop QCF plus-density reproduces PIXEL's stored forward Mellin coefficient: the plus-moment equals -_pseudoitd_nlo_moments(N, lam=1.37).
tests.actual: Quadrature-integrates li_vector_densities(lam=1.37, nf=3, n_points=128)'s p1 against (z**(N-1) - 1) for N=1..5 and compares to -_pseudoitd_nlo_moments(orders, lam=1.37).real.
tests.how: Two independent representations of the same one-loop constant: a z-space HPL density integrated numerically (translated from Li-Ma-Qiu, arXiv:2401.16281) versus a closed-form complex-N digamma/trigamma expression written years earlier for the Mellin route. Neither is derived from the other.
tests.catches: Added by the concurrent NNLO session; documented here 2026-08-13 while closing weakness -03, because it is the link that carries the external ancillary benchmark onto _pseudoitd_nlo_moments. Measured by mutation 2026-08-13: corrupting the L(N) constant inside _pseudoitd_nlo_moments fails this test AND the harmonic-sum test but NOT the ancillary benchmark; perturbing the Li p10 density by 1e-6 relative fails this test AND the ancillary benchmark but NOT the harmonic-sum tests. Both links are therefore load-bearing in the direction claimed.

tests.name: test_li_vector_formula_matches_authors_ancillary_iA_benchmark
tests.claim: PIXEL's translated temporal-vector QCF densities reproduce the authors' own Mathematica output for iA(omega=29.15), nf=3, at both one and two loops.
tests.actual: Reconstructs the unnormalized QCF from _li_vector_quadrature(192)'s raw density components and compares the two NLO and three NNLO alpha_s^n L^k coefficients to literals copied from the ancillary notebook.
tests.how: The comparison values come from papers/.../Li-Ma-Qiu_Extraction-NNLO-Parton-Distribution-Functions-from-Lattice-QCD/attachedfiels/readme.nb, Out[16] (verified present on disk 2026-08-13). This is an external oracle: nothing in PIXEL produced those numbers. It exercises every positive- and negative-support function before the reduced-ratio normalization, so a transcription error cannot cancel in a shared quotient.
tests.catches: Added by the concurrent NNLO session; documented here 2026-08-13 while closing weakness -03. Measured by mutation 2026-08-13: scaling p10 by 1.000001 fails it. It is independent of _pseudoitd_nlo_moments -- corrupting that function's L(N) constant leaves this test passing -- which is exactly why it can serve as the anchor of the chain.

tests.name: test_generation_time_build_matches_the_fitting_time_forward_operator
tests.claim: build_pseudoitd(..., with_systematics=False), the generation-time invocation, changes only the nuisance list -- not the forward operator and not the data.
tests.actual: Builds the same manifest record both ways and asserts len(contributions) is 1 versus 1 + len(record['systematics']), that the physical kernel is still EvolvedPseudoITD, that the two kernels' _cache_settings() dicts are equal, and that mean/cov/nu are array-equal.
tests.how: A3, an identity between two objects this suite builds. _cache_settings() is the twenty-key dict the code itself uses to decide kernel cache identity, so two kernels agreeing on it are the same operator by the code's own definition -- cheaper and no weaker than assembling two 128-node matrices.
tests.catches: Measured by mutation 2026-08-13: a PseudoITD.from_file that drops mu0_2/evolution_lambda/matching when systematics is None -- i.e. the evolution dict made conditional on with_systematics, the coupling the audit named -- leaves the generating build's kernel a bare Cosine and fails both items, while every other test in the file passes.

tests.name: test_evolved_pseudoitd_refuses_a_grid_with_a_node_at_the_origin
tests.claim: EvolvedPseudoITD.base_matrix raises on a basis whose first node is exactly 0.0, and the origin node is the whole cause.
tests.actual: pytest.raises(ValueError, match='node at x=0') on CubicSplineBasis([0.0, *geomspace(1e-3, 1, 8)]), with a control on CubicSplineBasis(geomspace(1e-3, 1, 8)) run all the way to a finite matrix. The two node arrays are asserted array_equal after the origin.
tests.how: F1, structural. Matched on the message rather than the type, because this method raises ValueError from four different guards. Grid's own node placement never lands on 0.0 (checked 2026-08-13: Grid(n_points=9, domain=(0.0, 1.0), spacing='linear') starts at 0.0025), which is why a raw-node CubicSplineBasis is needed.
tests.bar: exception type + message substring; control asserts shape, finiteness and a nonzero maximum
tests.catches: Measured by mutation 2026-08-13: a basis_grid_nodes that silently strips a leading zero (the plausible 'work around it instead of refusing' bug) fails this test and nothing else; so does a guard that raises with a different message, which is what the message match buys. Cost ~0.7 s -- LO with matching off, since the guard fires before matching_scales is called.

STILL OPEN, and out of scope for a test file: matching.py:382-414 still carries no literature citation, unlike its neighbour _pitd_gluon_finite_moments. That is a src/ docstring edit. src/pixel/kernels/matching.py:382-414 (_pseudoitd_nlo_moments) carries no literature citation, unlike its neighbor _pitd_gluon_finite_moments (matching.py:421-459), which cites Balitsky-Morris-Radyushkin PRD 105, 014008 (2022) Eq. weaknesses.why_it_matters: both tests recompute the identical B(N)/L(N) algebraic combination via harmonic sums, independent of the source's digamma calls but not of the underlying formula; a transcription error in the physics content (as opposed to the digamma bookkeeping) would reproduce identically in the harmonic-sum recomputation and pass both tests. weaknesses.proposed_fix: cite the source paper/equation for the non-singlet pseudo-ITD one-loop matching constant in matching.py's docstring (out of scope for this file); once a citation exists, add a value copied directly from the paper as a third check.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by adding the explicit atol=0.0 to test_matching_log_carries_the_lambda_dependence's np.allclose, so the coded rtol=1e-12 is now the operative bar rather than numpy's default atol=1e-8. Oracle: A3, the same manifest record built both ways, compared through EvolvedPseudoITD._cache_settings() -- the dict the code itself uses for kernel cache identity, so agreement on it IS operator identity by the code's own definition -- plus array-equality on mean/cov/nu, which catches a flag that also dropped a covariance block. Acceptance: an in-memory PseudoITD.from_file that drops mu0_2/evolution_lambda/matching when systematics is None (the coupling this item worried about) leaves the generating build's kernel a bare Cosine and fails both items, and nothing else in the file notices. closure_JAM_truth/datasets.py's module docstring (lines 1-22) states generation builds physical-only datasets (with_systematics=False) and injects systematics separately, while fitting uses with_systematics=True; both must produce the identical forward operator for the closure to be meaningful. Every call in this file (e.g. tests/test_closure_pseudoitd_matching.py line 205's datasets.build_pseudoitd(record, path, fields, None)) leaves with_systematics at its True default. Reading the source shows the evolution dict construction (closure_JAM_truth/datasets.py:108-116) is unconditional on with_systematics, so no coupling bug currently exists, but that decoupling is not verified by any test.
missing.proposed_location: tests/test_closure_pseudoitd_matching.py (a with_systematics=False variant of test_pitd_evolve_constant_reaches_the_built_kernels checking the main kernel is still EvolvedPseudoITD with the same attributes, and that len(contributions) == 1)
searched: grep -rn with_systematics tests/test_*.py | grep -i pseudo -> 0 hits

grep -rn build_pseudoitd tests/test_*.py closure_JAM_truth/*.py closure_NNPDF_truth/*.py -> only tests/test_closure_pseudoitd_matching.py (3 call sites, all default with_systematics=True) and the _LATTICE_BUILDERS dispatch dict in both suites' datasets.py (internal use by generate.py/fit.py, not exercised by any test directly)

notes_for_readme: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-13. The earlier note said the pseudo-ITD one-loop matching constant had no independent physics oracle anywhere in the suite or in fitpack_legacy/pdf_fitter. That was true when written and is no longer: the concurrent NNLO session's Li-vector work supplies one, anchored on the authors' own Mathematica ancillary output and carried onto _pseudoitd_nlo_moments by the Li-to-Mellin bridge test in this file. Both links were verified independent by mutation (see weakness -03). What remains missing is a literature CITATION in matching.py's docstring, which is a src/ edit, not a test.
